questions.stem: What is the balanced equation for the reaction of hydrogen with oxygen to form water?
questions.explanation: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O is balanced: 4 hydrogen atoms and 2 oxygen atoms on each side. You must not change the formulae of the substances, only add coefficients.

questions.stem: When balancing equations, which of the following can you change?

options.text: The large numbers (coefficients) in front of formulae
The subscript numbers in chemical formulae
The chemical symbols of the elements

questions.explanation: When balancing equations, you can only change the large numbers (coefficients) in front of formulae. You must never change subscript numbers as this would change the substance itself.

questions.stem: What coefficient should be placed in front of Fe to balance: Fe + O₂ → Fe₂O₃?
questions.explanation: The balanced equation is 4Fe + 3O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃. This gives 4 iron atoms and 6 oxygen atoms on each side.

questions.stem: Which state symbol represents a substance dissolved in water?
questions.explanation: (aq) stands for aqueous, meaning dissolved in water. The other state symbols are (s) for solid, (l) for liquid, and (g) for gas.

questions.stem: Balance the equation: Na + H₂O → NaOH + H₂
questions.explanation: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂ is balanced: 2 Na, 4 H, and 2 O atoms on each side.

questions.stem: In the equation Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂, how many hydrogen atoms are on the reactant side?
questions.explanation: 2HCl means there are 2 molecules of HCl, each containing 1 hydrogen atom. So there are 2 hydrogen atoms on the reactant side, matching the 2 in H₂ on the product side.

questions.stem: Why must chemical equations be balanced?

options.text: Because the number of molecules must be equal on both sides
Because atoms cannot be created or destroyed in chemical reactions
Because all reactions produce equal amounts of products and reactants
Because it is a scientific convention with no real meaning

questions.explanation: Equations must be balanced because of the law of conservation of mass - atoms cannot be created or destroyed. Every atom present in the reactants must also be present in the products.
